title: Subagent transcripts skip image externalization before size cap / redaction

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers the sanitize/size-cap ordering in prepareSubagentTranscript, but nothing mentions image externalization being deliberately omitted for subagent transcripts. The omission appears to be a gap, not a chosen behaviour.

evidence.text:
fix(checkpoint): measure the sanitized subagent transcript against the cap

Trail finding 019ff2bc: the size guard compared the raw byte count to
MaxChunkSize before sanitizing, so a Codex rollout that is oversized only because
of encrypted_content — up to ~20% of a rollout's bytes, per the measurement in
the same doc comment — was dropped entirely even though what would actually be
stored fits comfortably. The finding is right, and it contradicted the rationale
written two lines above the check.

Sanitize first, then measure what would be stored. Sanitizing costs ~8ms/MB
against the ~220ms/MB redaction this guard exists to bound, so paying it before
the decision is cheap even when the answer is still "skip". The warning now logs
both sizes, so a genuine skip shows how much of it survived sanitizing.

TestPrepareSubagentTranscript_MeasuresSanitizedSize covers it with a rollout
whose ciphertext alone pushes it past the cap; verified RED against the old
ordering ("a rollout that fits once encrypted_content is stripped must not be
dropped").
